text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
Robusta futures in London closed higher following New York. March added $61 to close at $1,791 per tonne, while May closed $51 higher at $1,768 per tonne.
The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) said it would hold a technical meeting on March 20 in London to review the surge in world coffee prices.

Arabica futures in New York closed higher across the board with front month March gaining 3.50 cents/lb to close at 219.00 cents/lb, while May closed 3.85 cents/lb higher at 203.15 cents/lb. Ongoing concerns about tight supplies and prospects of supplies becoming tighter yet in the next quarter should keep the market in a steep uptrend, traders said.

Export data continue to show extremely heavy shipments this quarter and this coffee seems to be readily absorbed with market actions suggesting it has not been enough to satisfy buyers, it was added. It is feared, that export volumes will decline sharply next quarter due to this front loading of shipments.
However, with only a week left to go before the spot March contract goes off the board, its open interest is still relatively high at 1,131 lots, or the equivalent of about 300,000 bags of coffee.

BRAZIL - According to the Brazilian Federation of Coffee Exporters (Febec) coffee exports doubled in the first two months of 1997 compared to the same period the year before. Total coffee exports in February reached 1.085 million bags, down from 1.243 million bags the previous month.
That brought total shipments since the beginning of 1997 up to 2.328 million bags, up from 1.183 million bags exported the same two months in 1996.

Total export earnings in January/February 1997 reached $324 million, up from $161 million the same period in 1996. The coffee bean price rose 19 per cent to $152 per bag in February versus $139 in January.
UNITED STATES - The USDA will not be issuing a Brazilian coffee estimate on March 12 as they normally would have. The next estimate will probably be in June.

DENMARK - Denmark imported 85,422 bags of coffee in December 1996, nearly 13 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports in calendar year 1996 up to 1.008 million bags, 15 per cent more than was imported the previous year. Main suppliers of green coffee in 1996 were Brazil (283,500 vs 315,800 bags) and Colombia (212,500 vs 183,700 bags). The country exported 108,100 bags of coffee 1996, nearly 19 per cent more than the 91,200 bags shipped in 1995.

TAIWAN - Taiwan imported 20,900 bags of coffee in November 1996, up from 16,500 bags imported the previous month. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 193,600 bags. Taiwan imports most of its coffee in the form of solubles. The largest supplier in January/November 1996 was South Korea with 37,800 bags.
